Eight ways to hold ground on this coast Most enquiries start with a fall the owner cannot use and a rough idea of a material. The useful order is the other way round: height, what sits above the wall, the ground and the drainage first, then the material. A concrete sleeper wall between galvanised posts suits most replacement work. A timber sleeper terrace still earns its place on a low garden fall. Core-filled besser block handles the tall, rendered and engineered jobs. A rock wall battered back into the slope suits acreage with room behind the face, and a gabion basket structure suits scour and surface runoff on erodible ground. Behind every one of them sits the same subsoil drainage requirement, and above the taller ones sits an engineered retaining wall pathway with AS 4678 design, Form 15 and Form 16. View service -> Why people use us on a wall decision QBCC-licensed specialists Retaining wall work across the Sunshine Coast is carried out by licensed contractors in our network. Licensing is triggered by the value of the work, not the height of the wall. Council approval understood upfront Sunshine Coast Council requires a building permit before construction, modification or repair of most retaining walls, and its own approval as a concurrence agency for walls over 2 metres. We work that out with you before anything is quoted. Drainage treated as structural Subsoil drainage behind the wall is a requirement, not a finishing touch. Poor drainage is the leading cause of wall failure, so ag drain, aggregate and geofabric are part of every scope we discuss. Built for Sunshine Coast ground Blackall Range basalt clay, Buderim volcanic soil, Landsborough sandstone and coastal dune sand each behave differently. The right wall for a Maleny slope is not the right wall for a Peregian Springs sand ridge. Which trade do you actually need? People ask for a bricklayer, a landscaper, a mason or someone with an excavator for the same job. The line that matters is not the trade name: QBCC licensing is triggered by the value of the building work, not by the height of the wall. Structural retaining walls are Class 10b structures designed to AS 4678, and an engineered wall is typically certified by an RPEQ via Form 15 for the design and Form 16 on inspection. The specialists in our network hold the licence and carry out the work. Retaining wall cost per metre, and what really moves it Walls are priced by square metre of wall face, which is height multiplied by length. A wall 1.2 metres high and 10 metres long is 12 square metres of face, not 10 metres of wall. Indicative bands run from around $150 to $300 per square metre for rock and boulder walls, $300 to $450 for timber sleepers, $250 to $430 for gabion, $550 to $700 for concrete sleepers and $550 to $750 for core-filled block.
